root_idea.summary: The root is oriented toward whiteness or brightness in a thing, exemplified by the moon and by white or moon-coloured objects.
root_idea.development: From this brightness principle, the lexicon develops terms for the moon, moonlight, lunar colour, and effects of moonlight such as dazzled sight. Gambling vocabulary is also attested under the root, although its derivation from the brightness principle is disputed.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed as the normalized singular noun قَمَر, the canonical Quranic form meaning the moon.

senses.definition: The moon, the lunar body and night luminary.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quran uses the noun for the moon in contexts of its light, phases, rising, appointed courses, and extraordinary events such as its splitting; case, definiteness, and prepositional variation do not create separate lexical senses.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To have one's sight dazzled or obscured by moonlight or snow, becoming unable to see properly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a person or animal, or of the sight itself, when bright moonlight or snow impairs vision.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become sleepless in the moonlight.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional use describing a person kept awake by moonlight.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To gamble or contend with someone for stakes and overcome him in the game.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with games, gaming implements, or property as the object of a wager.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To contend with someone for stakes or wagers; to gamble with him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Refers to a game of hazard or another game in which the winner receives something from the loser.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the new moon, to become a قَمَر at the stage called the third night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of the moon's early monthly development.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become moonlit or bright with moonlight; of a night, to become bright, or of people, to enter upon moonlight as the moon rises.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a night or of people entering the period of moonlight.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To wait for or watch for the rising of the moon.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal use describing anticipation of moonrise.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To come or go in the moonlight; especially, to pursue or hunt animals or birds in it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In hunting descriptions, the moonlight may dazzle the pursued animals' sight; the construction also describes a predator going out in moonlight in search of prey.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To deceive, beguile, or circumvent someone, intending harm without making its source apparent.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative or idiomatic transitive use distinct from movement in moonlight.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To gamble together or play a game of hazard for stakes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal construction describing several parties contending for wagers.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Nighttime in which livestock are left to pasture without a keeper.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Occurs in the expression for leaving cattle to graze unattended at night, contrasted with doing so by day in the sun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The sun and the moon considered together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dual expression in which one of the two may be grammatically or rhetorically predominant.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A diminutive name for the moon; conventionally, the moon during the dark interval called مُحَاق.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The specialized phase sense belongs to the diminutive expression rather than creating a separate sense of the Quranic noun قَمَر.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A colour ranging from greenish or dingy white to clear or pure whiteness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term describes a colour quality whose exact shade is variously specified as dusky, dingy, or bright white.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Lunar; of or relating to the moon.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used attributively, as in a lunar year.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A particular bird, especially a collared turtle-dove or related pigeon of a dull whitish colour.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word is also used in feminine and plural forms for the corresponding bird group; its derivation is explained variously in the lexical tradition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A game of hazard or gambling for stakes.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes games such as مَيْسِر and other games in which the winner receives something from the loser.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An opponent or participant in a gambling contest.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is reported as أَقْمَار, an anomalous plural formation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Moon-coloured, white, or intensely white; by extension, moonlike in the whiteness of a face, and of clouds, bright white and full of water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The colour may be described as dull, dusky, or greenish-tinged white; the cloud use associates intense brightness with abundance of water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A moonlit night or moonlight itself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a night in which the moon shines and in expressions meaning to sit or come in the moonlight.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In a proverbial expression, to have the light of the moon, meaning to wait patiently for the fulfilment of one's need.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is an idiomatic proverbial interpretation, not a separate literal sense of moonlight.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a waterskin, to become spoiled or damaged through exposure to moonlight.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized intransitive use describing deterioration attributed to moonlight.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To deceive someone and divert or deprive him of something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic transitive use in which the object is deceived away from the matter in question.

cautions: The derivation of the gambling vocabulary from the root's whiteness or brightness principle is explicitly disputed; the gambling meanings themselves are independently attested.
Classical sources vary in the precise lunar phase denoted by some specialized expressions, while the Quranic form قَمَر is used broadly for the moon.
